verification.contract: The Go helper corpus_manifest.go re-derives digest, byte size and intrinsic count for every digest-bearing entry — synthetic-seed AND frozen producer-pinned rows — and refuses producer-pinned entries that are still acquisition-pending but have bytes on disk.

generator.regeneration: synthetic-seed entries are byte-deterministic: a re-run reproduces the frozen sha256 digests exactly; drift fails `verify` and the Go test
generator.acquisition: `scripts/gen-meet-m0-corpus.sh acquire` stages the five producer-pinned conversions through the pinned engine (SOFFICE env or PATH) into a staging dir and prints a digest/size/count fragment for the manifest update + dated receipt. This is the linux-ci-host re-qualification procedure; it never overwrites frozen corpus rows.

classSemantics.producer-pinned: Bytes produced by the D3-pinned producer (LibreOffice headless, MPL-2.0) with the engine identity captured verbatim from `soffice --version` at generation time. Producer versions are NEVER invented; entries stay 'acquisition-pending' until that capture happens. Revision 2 captured the engine dev-side on darwin/arm64 (owner-directed 2026-09-20 qualification run); the linux-ci-host server-side capture remains the production-pin follow-up and re-runs the same recipes with a fresh dated receipt.
classSemantics.synthetic-seed: Deterministic in-repo generated fixtures (scripts/gen-meet-m0-corpus.sh, no network, no third-party material). They carry structure, size and counts for bandwidth benchmarking and serve as LibreOffice conversion INPUTS. They are NEVER passable as producer-pinned evidence and are never renderer-qualification inputs.

r2MeasurementProtocol.frozenBy: M0: 'M0 freezes the 20-page reference deck and R2 measurement protocol. Five exploratory 30-minute runs inform feasibility only.'
r2MeasurementProtocol.scope: Document/presentation lane only (corpus bytes, manifests, page events, prefetch, captions/timeline). Media-quality non-inferiority and total endpoint traffic are separate named lanes measured on the media path, not with these fixtures.
methodInvariants: Every claimed cache/network cell needs the specified 20 randomized pairs.
Attributed transfer accounting: bytes are attributed to document / media / control classes; document claims use document-attributed bytes only.
One-sided confidence bounds on every claim; point estimates alone never admit a cell.
Five exploratory 30-minute runs inform feasibility only and never count as pass evidence.
Missing, skipped, or flaky-after-retry runs never count as passes (repo verification discipline).

benchmarks.planBudget: Presentation GA requires at least 80% less attributed document transfer
benchmarks.metric: percent reduction of document-attributed transfer bytes, cached vs uncached
benchmarks.passRule: one-sided lower bound of the reduction >= 80% for the GA claim; 10x stretch claimed only if measured

benchmarks.metric: meeting elapsed time where cumulative attributed cost of cached mode drops below uncached mode
benchmarks.passRule: reported with confidence interval; no threshold

benchmarks.planBudget: Initial manifest target under 256 KiB for 500 pages; larger metadata paginates
benchmarks.metric: serialized meet-pages-v1 Manifest bytes for all 500 pages of m0corpus-pdf-large-500p.pdf
benchmarks.passRule: bytes < 262144 (rendition.go MaxManifestBytes); above it, pagination MUST engage

benchmarks.planBudget: Default prefetch is current + next two pages, bounded by 24 MiB and reduced under constrained connectivity. Audio/video health has priority over page prefetch.
benchmarks.metric: sum of encoded page-asset bytes in the current+2 prefetch window; aggregate resident bytes under eviction pressure
benchmarks.passRule: window sum <= 25165824 (rendition.go MaxEncodedClientAssetsBytes); the asset-heavy fixture's 28.3 MiB aggregate forces the bounding path to be observable, not assumed

benchmarks.planBudget: Admitted API/stored event objects at most 16KiB; complete serialized LiveKit envelopes at most 14000 UTF-8 bytes; page-change payload target under1KiB
benchmarks.metric: serialized page-change payload, stored event object, and full envelope bytes under the densest page content
benchmarks.passRule: payload < 1024 target; stored <= 16384; envelope <= 14000 UTF-8 bytes (envelope.go NewEnvelope refuses over-budget frames)

benchmarks.planBudget: Cached-reference-deck start p95 is at most 30 seconds
benchmarks.metric: start-to-first-page-visible latency, warm cache, p95 over randomized pairs

benchmarks.planBudget: newly accepted rendition start p95 is at most 90 seconds on the reference stack. Fallback is reachable in at most two interactions and does not end the meeting or accepted recording.
benchmarks.metric: accept-to-start latency on a cold rendition, p95
benchmarks.passRule: p95 <= 90 s; fallback reachability asserted behaviourally (two interactions, session/recording preserved)

benchmarks.planBudget: Reducer page-change p95 under 150 ms and data-channel visible convergence p95 under 300 ms on the reference LAN, excluding page asset download
benchmarks.metric: reducer commit latency p95; convergence latency p95 (asset download excluded by protocol)
benchmarks.passRule: reducer p95 < 150 ms; convergence p95 < 300 ms

benchmarks.planBudget: Semantic replay streams timeline/media indexes; it does not load all media or annotations into memory
benchmarks.metric: peak resident memory while streaming a replay whose timeline references all 5000 caption cues and 800 annotations
benchmarks.passRule: streaming asserted (no full materialization); absolute memory bound named in the M4 slice owning replay
